calls.reason: There is no deadline, and the evidence shows only isolated fixes: OpenAI's sycophancy rollback and Google's narrow removal of health summaries, with other flagged problems persisting. That is not the broad change the forecast predicts.

The Stanford/Harvard study of selected pages shows large exposure to AI images, and the First Monday pilot used only four accounts. Neither measures what share of typical Facebook feeds was AI slop in December 2024.

NIST says detection is limited, but the SynthID watermark paper shows working automated detection for marked text. Human accuracy ranges from chance to strong, so neither the human exception nor unavoidability is established.

CNBC's report of OpenAI's projected $5 billion loss backs the burning-billions part for one company. OpenAI's credit line was undrawn, and nothing shows industry over-leverage or no path to profitability.
